regime_context: The detector shows a narrow (39% eligible, narrowing), leadership split between Memory/HBM (rank 1) and Big Pharma (rank 2), with Big Pharma flagged as the headline and crowded. The validated edge here is only the absolute-trend gate for drawdown/shake-out control; cross-sectional rank is a focus lens, not alpha. We have a modest track record (dir_accuracy 0.41), so I keep conviction low throughout.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Defensives (rank 4, eligible, durability 0.82, breadth 0.944, but crowded z=1.45) can sustain its trend leg as a diversifier against the crowded healthcare leadership. I would retire this watch if XLP or XLU rolls over and loses its 20-day moving average while Big Pharma continues higher — that would signal defensive participation is not confirming the risk-off rotation.

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the headline, ranked #2, eligible, with strong durability (0.84), full breadth (1.0), hurst_tag 'trend', and val_state 'confirming'. It is the clearest durable trend in the eligible set. Crowding (z=1.46) is a size-down caution only, not a fade call. The trend-gate leg supports staying long until the trend breaks.
theses.dissent: Crowding z=1.46 and full breadth mean much of the good news may be priced; healthcare names can de-rate quickly on policy headlines (unscheduled_share=1.0 in macro flow).

falsifier.text: PPH closes below its 50-day moving average and prints a lower weekly low before the check-by date

theses.subject: Health Care (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Health Care (Equal-Weight) is eligible with high durability (0.78), trend hurst, and broad participation (0.917). It is a second, more diversified expression of the same defensive-healthcare leadership already in Big Pharma. Crowding is high (z=1.54), so this is a hold/lean rather than a chase.
theses.dissent: Very crowded; the equal-weight sector is highly correlated with the headline crowded Big Pharma theme, so this adds little diversification and could fall with it.

falsifier.text: XLV lags SPY by more than 3% over the next 10 trading days
